nodes.notes: A row another run is already working is skipped. A claim older than STALE_CLAIM_MINUTES (30 when unset) is treated as abandoned, so a run that died cannot strand an application forever.

nodes.name: Claim the row for the summary
nodes.notes: A compare-and-swap, not a hopeful write. The second condition is the value this run just read, null included, so only one of several runs can match. A conditional update that matches nothing returns an empty result and emits no items, which silently skips the row. Two runs overlapping is how one application got two summaries in its thread. It also bounds a row whose Slack parent post failed: with no thread anchor its summary is discarded at the end, and the claim turns that from a README fetch and a model call on every tick into one attempt per stale window.
